There's a stretch behind you where nothing wanted to grow, and you arranged your life around making that feel like a choice. The caring is still in you — you feel it nowhere. You stopped turning toward what used to draw you, and staying steady has come to look like being free of wants. It isn't the same thing. You're further from yourself than the door you're at.

What pulls forward doesn't come from effort. It comes from wants — the light you'd steer by if you let yourself. Face a thing you once wanted and stay with the pull of it, to yourself, before you decide anything about it. A direction to face is enough to start.
3.sheetLine: You're at the door, and it's behind you.

4.tense: You've been the one people lean on for a long time, and you'd call it just how you are.
4.verb: tending what's growing without forcing it
4.place: where what's already in you comes out and shows
4.ask: There's upkeep you do for other people that you didn't sign up for. Drop that upkeep for a week — no announcement, no explanation. Leave it and notice what your hands feel like.
4.core:
Somewhere along the way you became the one who holds things up for others, and by now it feels like your shape rather than a choice. People bring you what they can't carry and you take it, and you talk about it like it's simply how things are. The caring is real — it's why they come. You'd say you're fine. Something in you keeps mentioning that you're tired.

There's a point where holding stops being care and becomes what's left over. Take one piece of upkeep you do for others that you didn't agree to carry, and stop doing it for a week. Don't announce it. Put it down and see what's still in your hands.
4.sheetLine: You hold it up for them and call it just you.

1.tense: The whole pattern is coming into view and you are letting it unfold at its own pace.
1.verb: tending what is growing without forcing it
1.place: seeing the whole pattern from inside it
1.ask: Look across the whole picture this week: notice one habit it no longer needs, then release it deliberately, hands open, nothing slipping past you.
1.core:
Seeing the whole of something and letting it grow without your hand on it are the same act here. You hold the full shape of what you are tending and you keep your grip loose, so what wants to develop can. The pattern tells you what it needs; you give that and stop there. Nothing in you is pushing for it to become something else.

The next piece is subtraction. Before this week's pattern goes anywhere, sit with it and let one true thing come clear that does not belong to what is growing — a habit, an expectation, a hand you kept on it. Then release it deliberately, fully, and put it behind you. The whole shape stays easier to see without it, and it does not need to be replaced.
1.sheetLine: You see the whole pattern and your hand stays loose.

2.tense: Tomorrow's version of this is already in your hands, and you are tending it before it exists.
2.verb: tending what is growing without forcing it
2.place: seeing the whole pattern from inside it
2.ask: Start the next move on what is growing only as far as the light reaches — one step, then stop; let the rest stay dark a while.
2.core:
Care has become holding. The whole pattern is in view, and along with it every way it could go wrong, so the work has turned into steering — checking, correcting, getting out in front of how it will develop. The shape is being protected from outcomes it cannot have yet. Nothing you are doing is careless. It is just running past the thing itself, working from a picture instead of from what is here.

Take one step at a time, and only where the light reaches. Not the whole route, not the next three turns. One step, then stop. The rest stays unclear until it isn't. What is living gets to make its own timing.
2.sheetLine: You hold the shape too hard before it can grow.

3.tense: Standing at a door already closed, wondering why you never walked through it.
3.verb: tending what is growing without forcing it
3.place: seeing the whole pattern from inside it
3.ask: Take up the one you would grieve to lose, and make a small move toward it this week — named, yours, unexplained.
3.core:
Nothing much has been growing, and you have a name for that: you are fine on your own, you do not need much, you keep to yourself. The independence is real. So is the pattern underneath it, which sees the whole and holds itself outside of it. You are separate and you are safe and the door stays shut. That is not a failure of care. It is care pointed at the closed door instead of through it.

What is missing is a want that is yours and out in the open. Settle on what you would be genuinely sorry to lose — not to have, eventually, if — and take one step toward it, small and by name. The step is the whole act. Let the direction move you.
3.sheetLine: You see the whole pattern and hold yourself outside it.

4.tense: Others named you caretaker and you have held that shape without noticing you raised your hand.
4.verb: tending what is growing without forcing it
4.place: seeing the whole pattern from inside it
4.ask: When the pattern calls and your hands go to it, wait — see who chose this — then set down a piece that wasn't yours to carry.
4.core:
You are seen as the one who tends. That was assigned, mostly, and you have been carrying it as though it were simply your shape — sitting with it, holding space for whoever arrives, keeping the whole pattern running. What looks like your nature is a role with a hand in it. The choice is unclaimed and the weariness is the cost of holding something you did not pick up.

The act is not to stop caring. The act is to notice your hand on it. Each time you step into the caretaker slot just because it is open, take one second to see you are doing it, and then set down a piece — not because it collapsed, because you chose. The role is smaller when it is chosen. It can be.
4.sheetLine: You are caretaker by assignment and by an unclaimed hand.

1.tense: The care moves at the speed of what it tends, and nothing is being pushed.
1.verb: tending what is still growing, without forcing it
1.place: where what has been made is finished and let go
1.ask: Keep doing the part that is yours, and stop checking whether it's working. Give it a week in which the result is not measured, not inspected, not gone over.
1.core:
The care you give is patient with what it tends. You make the conditions and then you wait, and the waiting is not passive — it's the part that lets a thing come up straight instead of hothouse-fast. People can tell being tended from being managed, and with you they get tended, and most of them can't name the difference when they feel it.

At some point your work is done and the outcome belongs to the thing itself. That point arrives quietly, and this week you can practise noticing it. Hand the result over instead of resting a hand on it, and stay nearby without holding on. Letting go will not feel like losing. It'll feel like your hands are free for what comes next, which is what finishing is for.
1.sheetLine: You tend what's growing at its own speed, and it holds.

2.tense: The care is already braced for a future that hasn't happened yet and may not.
2.verb: tending what is still growing, without forcing it
2.place: where what has been made is finished and let go
2.ask: Don't arrange anyone's outcome today. Work with just the light you have — the next hour — and leave the shape unfinished, so the rest can arrive when it arrives.
2.core:
The care has picked up speed. You can see what a thing could become and you are already there, arranging it, shielding it from a season it hasn't met. It reads as devotion from the outside. From where you stand it's closer to holding something so tightly your arms have gone numb, and the thing in them can't move either.

Not knowing isn't the enemy. Most of what you're bracing for won't arrive, and the parts that do don't need your answer today. Enough light for the next step is enough. Give the future its uncertainty back; your grip loosens, and this starts feeding you again instead of emptying the day.
2.sheetLine: The care has taken on a job it can't finish.

3.tense: The tending stopped, and the hands that did it are standing at a door that's closed.
3.verb: tending what is still growing, without forcing it
3.place: where what has been made is finished and let go
3.ask: Take one small step toward something you actually want, for no one else. It doesn't need a plan — a single step toward it is enough.
3.core:
Where things get made, nothing is being made right now. You keep your distance well, and it reads as self-sufficiency, but at that distance nothing grows in your hands. People ask less of you than they used to, which is its own relief, and also its own kind of empty. Nothing in you is aimed anywhere at the moment.

There is a pull in you that hasn't been out in a while. It doesn't need a route, just a direction, and directions are cheap — you can choose one and set it down if it's wrong. Pick the thing whose loss you'd feel most, and face it once, without arranging the whole way there first. Wanting something, even only to yourself, is how the pull gets its current back.
3.sheetLine: You've kept your distance so well that nothing grows in your hands.

4.tense: The caring happens through your hands, and you didn't sign anything that says it's yours.
4.verb: tending what is still growing, without forcing it
4.place: where what has been made is finished and let go
4.ask: Set down a load that isn't yours to carry — no checking on it, no fixing it — and leave that space open. Notice what, if anything, moves into it.
4.core:
In some part of your life people bring things to you, and you take them. You didn't apply for the job. You can carry a lot, so you do, and it shows up as the shape of your days rather than as a choice you made. What goes out doesn't come back in equal measure, and you've stopped expecting it to.

The way back starts with a no, and it doesn't have to be said to anyone. Set down a load that isn't yours, knowing it may go unnoticed and uncredited. Some loads get borne a long time without being named once. Setting this one down isn't abandoning anybody — it's finding out what you have when your hands belong to you again.
4.sheetLine: You're carrying things you didn't agree to carry.
